newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK OPPOSITION DEPUTY QUITS DEMOCRATIC UNION.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK OPPOSITION DEPUTY QUITS DEMOCRATIC UNION.

text.p: Slovak member of parliament Anton Hrnko has quit as a member of the opposition Democratic Union (DU) lowering the number of DU deputies in parliament to 14, the party said on Thursday.
Hrnko quit the right-wing Slovak National Party (SNS) in 1994, to help establish the DU along with former members of the Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) of Premier Vladimir Meciar.

The DU was instrumental in Meciar's ouster in March of 1994, but was relegated to the opposition after Meciar and HZDS won elections later that autumn and set up a broad coalition government along with the SNS.
In his letter of resignation, Hrnko said he had decided to quit after disagreements with both opposition and coalition policies, DU vice-chairman Jan Budaj, told Reuters.
Hrnko will stay on in parliament as an independent deputy until the next elections, he said.
"There were more points of difference between our (DU) ideas and those of Hrnko," Budaj said, but declined to elaborate.

DU party sources said the final step affecting his decision to quit the party was his opposition to the joint campaign by opposition parties for a petition setting up a referendum on allowing direct election of the president.
Hrnko was not available for comment.
